title: Control Artifact Capture Contract and Triage Playbook
body:
Purpose and scope

This working doc defines a capture contract for 'control artifacts' (the unit of record we push from service components into the evidence pipeline), the responsibilities of lightweight capture adapters (bridge adapters), and an operational triage playbook for failures and data gaps. The goal is a small, interoperable surface area that lets product teams emit verifiable artifacts without coupling to the SIEM or evidence store internals.

Why this is different from previous "evidence-*" designs
- Emphasis on a compact, transport-agnostic envelope (artifact-envelope) instead of large per-event schemas.
- Clear adapter contract boundaries: emit, ack, stash, retry; adapters must be replaceable without changing producers.
- Operational triage focused on end-to-end proof availability (not just log delivery).

High-level design decisions (summary)
- Minimal artifact envelope with explicit provenance fields and a small extensible metadata bag.
- Adapters translate local telemetry to artifact-envelope and push to an ingest gateway. Gateway validates and writes into the evidence-queue; downstream processors perform enrichment, fingerprinting, and SIEM mapping.
- Retain raw artifact message (immutable) for N days (configurable per tenant) and store fingerprints in the evidence index for longer-term auditability.

Artifact envelope (contract) — required fields
- artifact_id: stable UUID v4 assigned by producer (string)
- produced_at: ISO8601 timestamp in UTC
- producer: service name (e.g., serving-runtime.kernel-manager)
- artifact_type: enum (control-change, rbac-assert, audit-check, key-rotation, runbook-exec)
- severity: OPTIONAL enum (info, warning, critical) — used for routing to SIEM tiers
- provenance: simple string path (team/component/instance)
- payload_schema: short identifier (e.g., "rbac.v2.policy-change.v1")
- payload: opaque string or base64 for binary blobs (adapter-validated)
- signature: OPTIONAL hex string (ed25519) when producer has signing keys
- chain_hash: OPTIONAL SHA256 of previous artifact_id when producing a logical chain (helps chain-of-custody)
- retention_hint: OPTIONAL short (P30D, P365D) — consumer preference for TTL

Notes on schema choices
- Keep payload_schema small and namespaced; long/wide schemas make adapter translation brittle.
- Signature and chain_hash are optional to allow resource-constrained producers to emit without crypto; adapters/gateway can add signing when in dedicated deployments.

Adapter responsibilities (bridge-adapter contract)
- Accept local events from service (file, syslog, in-memory hook).
- Map local fields into artifact-envelope. Mapping must be explicit and stored in repo (example mapping YAML per service).
- Validate artifact-envelope locally (presence of artifact_id, produced_at, producer, payload_schema).
- Attach local adapter metadata: adapter_id, adapter_version, local_node_id.
- Batch to gateway with backoff. Each batch element returns an ack with ephemeral_ingest_id.
- On transient failure: buffer to local disk (bounded size), retry with exponential backoff, emit metric and alert when buffer > threshold.
- On permanent rejection (schema mismatch): write a rejection artifact to a dead-letter queue and create an auto-ticket with snapshot for triage.

Transport and gateway expectations
- Preferred transports: HTTPS (mutual TLS) to evidence-gateway, or gRPC with per-tenant credentials.
- Gateway performs lightweight validation and canonicalization, enriches with gateway_received_at, gateway_region, and writes into the evidence-queue (Kafka topic: evidence.ingest.v1).
- Gateway returns ingest status (accepted|rejected|deferred) and a canonical ingest_id. Adapters must log ingest_id and emit telemetry.

Ingest pipeline and SIEM export mapping
- Evidence-ingest -> enrichers (add identity, ip, KMS_key_id) -> fingerprinting (calculate SHA256 of payload) -> indexer (write to evidence-index) -> exporter(s)
- SIEM export is a downstream consumer that subscribes to a normalized topic: evidence.canonical.v1. Exporter maps artifact-envelope to SIEM event fields. Mapping rules must be stored and versioned in Git.
- Important mapping rules: artifact_type => SIEM.event.type, producer => SIEM.event.source, produced_at => SIEM.event.time, fingerprint => SIEM.event.fingerprint, signature => SIEM.event.crypto.signature

Retention, TTL, and data minimization
- Default warm retention: 30 days for raw artifacts. Long-term retention policy stores fingerprints and metadata for 3+ years.
- Sensitive payloads: adapters should drop PII before embedding in payload and instead link to secure vault entry (payload: {"vault_ref":"vault://keys/abcd"}).

Error classification and triage playbook
- Class A (producer misformat/permanent reject): blame producer mapping. Action: create OWNER ticket, attach sample event, immediate rollback guidance. Priority P1 if production control is impacted.
- Class B (gateway transient: downstream full/backpressure): adapters should automatically retry; SRE paged if queue lag > threshold for > 10m. Action: check evidence-gateway pods, auto-scale, inspect Kafka lag.
- Class C (data discrepancy / missing artifact proof): triage flow below.

Missing proof triage flow (step-by-step)
1) Verify ingest metrics: did gateway accept an event with producer and time window? Check adapter logs for ingest_id.
2) If ingest_id present, query evidence-index for fingerprint; verify indexer logs for enrichment errors.
3) If no ingest_id: check adapter buffer; did the adapter report local backpressure? Check adapter local disk for buffered batches.
4) If buffered batches exist: rehydrate and forward; escalate to owner if buffer > 1000 items or > 12 hours of backlog.
5) If adapter reports accepted but evidence-index missing: check downstream processor logs and Kafka consumer group offsets. If consumer lag, restart consumer & backfill.
6) If artifact exists but payload truncated or missing signature: treat as partial proof; consult product OWNER for acceptability and note in audit.

Operational runbook snippets (commands & hints)
- Check adapter status: kubectl -n svc-telemetry get pods -l app=evidence-adapter
- Tail adapter logs: kubectl logs -f <pod> -c adapter | grep ingest_id=<id>
- Check gateway: curl -k -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://evidence-gateway.internal/v1/health
- Kafka lag: kafkactl consumer-group-lag evidence-ingest-group --topic evidence.ingest.v1

On-call escalation matrix (quick)
- Adapter transient/backlog alert: eng-observability L2 (pager) -> adapter owner (team) -> SRE if > 30m unresolved.
- Gateway rejection spike (>1% rejection rate over 5m): security-compliance pager -> gateway-owner -> adapter owners for correlated schema changes.
- SIEM export mismatch (field mapping regression): security-compliance -> data-platform -> SIEM owners.

Samples (example envelope, single-line JSON representation):
{
  "artifact_id": "b2c9f4ae-8dbf-4d9b-bb3e-2a1f6a7d9c4f",
  "produced_at": "2026-02-25T17:03:11Z",
  "producer": "serving-runtime.kv-cache",
  "artifact_type": "control-change",
  "provenance": "platform/serving-runtime/instance-12",
  "payload_schema": "rbac.v2.policy-change.v1",
  "payload": "{\"actor\":\"ops@example.com\",\"change\":\"grant role X to user Y\"}",
  "signature": "",
  "retention_hint": "P365D"
}

Open design questions / TODOs
- Authorization model for adapters: should adapters authenticate using service identity or tenant-scoped API keys? Impact on rotation and secrets management.
- Gateway-signed artifacts: evaluate cost/benefit of having gateway sign canonical artifact for non-signing producers.
- Buffering guarantees: define exact durability SLA for local buffer (fsync semantics) across platforms (k8s ephemeral vs sidecar).
- SIEM export telemetry: need QA harness that verifies mapping rules against canonical test artifacts.

Appendix: quick checklist for teams integrating a new producer
- Add mapping YAML and example artifact to repo.
- Implement local validation and test harness (unit tests that run mapping).
- Deploy adapter in staging and watch ingest_id and evidence-index linkage.
- Run the SIEM export test harness to verify fields map correctly.
- Sign-off: security-compliance review and add retention_hint default.

Notes to self / next steps (internal)
- Sync with data-platform next week to finalize Kafka topic naming and retention configs.
- Wire up auto-ticketing for permanent rejections (JIRA bot prototype exists in repo).
- Build small demo (policy change -> artifact -> SIEM alert) for internal security review.

This doc intentionally mixes spec and runbook material so teams can get started quickly. Keep it lean: if something needs to be a full formal spec, extract and move to confluence once stable.
